arml-2023-relay-1-1.title: Add areas
arml-2023-relay-1-1.body:
$GH=22-5-5=12$. The hexagon consists of square $ABCD$, square $EFGH$ (outside, on side $GH$), and the two right triangles $AEH$ and $BFG$ with legs $5$ and $12$:
$$22^2+12^2+2\cdot\tfrac12\cdot5\cdot12=484+144+60=688.$$

**Answer: 688**

arml-2023-relay-1-2.title: Along the diagonal
arml-2023-relay-1-2.body:
*(In the relay, $T$ was the answer to the previous problem, 688.)*

Here $a=6$ and $b=8$. Let the small circle have center $Q$ and radius $\rho$. It is tangent to $MN$ and $MR$, so $Q$ lies on diagonal $MO$ with $MQ=\rho\sqrt2$. It is externally tangent to the circle of radius $a$ centered at $O$, so $OQ=a+\rho$ and (the tangent point lies on $MO$) $MO=MQ+OQ$:
$$b\sqrt2=\rho\sqrt2+\rho+a\ \Rightarrow\ \rho=\frac{b\sqrt2-a}{\sqrt2+1}=(b\sqrt2-a)(\sqrt2-1)=a+2b-(a+b)\sqrt2.$$
With $a=6$, $b=8$: $\rho=22-14\sqrt2$, so $x+y=22+14=36$.

**Answer: 36**

arml-2023-relay-1-3.title: Similar corner triangles
arml-2023-relay-1-3.body:
*(In the relay, $T$ was the answer to the previous problem, 36.)*

Let $s=\sqrt T=6$, $AM=a$, $AP=b$ (so $a^2+b^2=MP^2=4$). The four corner right triangles have hypotenuses the sides of the rectangle; from the right angles of $MNOP$, $\angle AMP=\angle BNM=\angle CON=\angle DPO$, so all four are similar, and by SAS $\triangle AMP\cong\triangle CON$, $\triangle BNM\cong\triangle DPO$. Then $BN=s-b$ and $BM=s-a$, and similarity $AMP\sim BNM$ gives $\frac a{s-b}=\frac b{s-a}$, i.e. $s(a-b)=(a+b)(a-b)$. So either $a=b$ or $a+b=s$.

If $a+b=6$ then $ab=\frac{36-4}2=16$, but $a+b\ge2\sqrt{ab}=8>6$ (AM-GM), impossible. So $a=b=\sqrt2$, and $\triangle BNM\sim\triangle AMP$ is an isosceles right triangle with $BM=BN=6-\sqrt2$, so
$$MN=\sqrt2\,(6-\sqrt2)=6\sqrt2-2.$$

**Answer: $6\sqrt2-2$**

arml-2023-relay-2-1.title: Match each half
arml-2023-relay-2-1.body:
There are $\binom{13}2=78$ ways to choose $2$ letters from each half. Ayesha must match Aditya's pair in both halves: the probability is $\frac1{78}\cdot\frac1{78}=\frac1{6084}$.

**Answer: $\frac1{6084}$**

arml-2023-relay-2-2.title: Powers of 2
arml-2023-relay-2-2.body:
*(In the relay, $T$ was the answer to the previous problem, $\frac1{6084}$.)*

We need $\frac1{2^n}<\frac1{6084}$, i.e. $2^n>6084$. Since $2^{12}=4096<6084<8192=2^{13}$, the least $n$ is $13$.

**Answer: 13**

arml-2023-relay-2-3.title: Discriminant
arml-2023-relay-2-3.body:
*(In the relay, $T$ was the answer to the previous problem, 13.)*

The roots are $\frac{13\pm\sqrt{169+4n}}2$, which are integers iff $169+4n$ is a perfect square $k^2$ with $k$ odd (same parity as $13$; any $k$ with $k^2=169+4n$ is automatically odd). With $n>2023$, $169+4n>8261$, and $90^2=8100<8261<8281=91^2$, so the least possible is $k=91$: $4n=8281-169=8112$, $n=2028$. (This is $>2023$ and $k=91$ is odd.)

**Answer: 2028**
